title: Horn Removal and Installation
introduction:
The horn assembly sits behind the left-hand fender splash shield—its wheel-arch raincoat. I approach this job from the outside in: remove the wheel, clear the shield, then disconnect and unbolt the horn. The illustration highlights the assembly in blue and its electrical connection and mounting bolt in magenta.

This guide covers removal and refitting, including the wheel-related preparation and completion work. It does not diagnose why a horn has stopped sounding or provide an electrical or operating test.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the vehicle. Otherwise, someone could remotely start it during service, causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting the engine; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Ignoring these precautions can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Prepare equipment and materials
items.detail: Have a suitable hoist, tools for the illustrated fasteners and retainers, and torque equipment for the horn bolt and wheel nuts. Use the wheel-pilot anti-seize specified in the materials table in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Read its material safety information sheet before use; improper use of service chemicals or materials can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Use the specified lifting points
items.detail: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Refer to [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation). Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame and use the corresponding points shown in the drawing. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Keep the parking brake applied for this horn job. If a related operation requires releasing it, first establish that all four wheels are fully clear of the ground and the vehicle is securely supported on the hoist.

items.name: Check hoist capacity and clearance
items.detail: The hoist must support the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Position its arms at the illustrated points. Keep adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage components. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and avoid damaging the axle or rear cover. Check for underbody interference before driving onto a drive-on lift. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are off the ground; incorrect arm positioning or ground contact can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Observe jack precautions if a jack is used during setup
items.detail: Use a jack with adequate capacity for the vehicle, cargo and modifications, on a hard, level surface at the specified lifting points. Set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. After jacking, support the vehicle with floor stands; never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, which can lower unexpectedly. Unintended movement can cause serious personal injury or death. The vehicle's supplied jack is only for an emergency deflated-tire change and must not be used for this repair. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper; bumper-cover damage will occur.

items.name: Use the wheel reference
items.detail: Review [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193) before beginning wheel work. Use [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) (204-04A Wheels and Tires, Removal and Installation) for removal and refitting. After safely positioning the vehicle on the hoist, remove the wheel nuts and remove the wheel-and-tire assembly.

items.name: Do not heat a seized wheel nut
items.detail: Heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Do not use it to loosen a seized nut.

items.name: Handle damaged wheels safely
items.detail: If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; otherwise, serious personal injury may result. Do not weld or peen a wheel. A wheel needing either repair must be replaced with a new wheel, because wheel failure can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Prepare the mounting faces
items.detail: Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting surface and the corresponding hub, brake drum or brake disc mounting surface. Secure any rotor-to-hub fasteners so they cannot interfere with those surfaces. Contamination or interference can let wheel nuts loosen and the wheel come off while driving, causing loss of control, serious injury or death.

items.name: Keep anti-seize confined to the pilot
items.detail: Apply a thin coat of the specified anti-seize only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot, as highlighted in the wheel illustration. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc/drum mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces; contact with those areas can damage components.

items.name: Seat and tighten the wheel
items.detail: Position the wheel and install the nuts finger tight initially. Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. As the tires meet the ground, restore wheel restraints to prevent rolling before final tightening. Perform final tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires. With clean, dry wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads, tighten in the illustrated star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Skipping that pattern can cause excessive brake-disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

items.name: Retighten after refitting
items.detail: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; failing to retighten can cause serious injury to vehicle occupants.

edits.text: NOTE: Removal steps may also contain installation details; keep those details in view when refitting the horn.
edits.why: The bolt specification appears alongside removal, but it governs tightening during installation.

edits.text:
Remove the LH (left-hand) fender splash shield.
Refer to: [Fender Splash Shield](#/document/G1693247) (501-02 Front End Body Panels, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The splash shield is the inner wheel-arch liner covering access to the horn. First remove the wheel and tire using the preparation above. Remove the retainers around the wheel-arch edge and underside, then remove the remaining retainers from the inner liner section. Check the top of the arch, the inboard liner edges and the lower flanges before removing the liner; underside attachments are easy to overlook. The linked shield reference shows their exact layout on the LH side and notes that RH is similar; this horn job specifically uses LH access.

edits.text:
Disconnect the horn electrical connector, then remove the mounting bolt and the horn assembly.
During installation, tighten the bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).
edits.why: I use the arrows to distinguish the electrical connector below the horn from the mounting bolt above it. Disconnecting the wiring first frees the assembly electrically before its mounting is released. The blue snail-shaped units belong to the illustrated horn assembly.

edits.text: Reverse the removal order: refit the horn assembly and mounting bolt, tighten the bolt to the specification in the removal step, and reconnect the electrical connector. Reinstall the splash shield and its retainers, then reinstall the wheel and tire using the wheel-installation requirements above.
edits.why: Reassembly closes the access route from the horn outward. I account for the horn mounting, electrical connection and shield attachments before completing wheel installation; the wheel's mounting-face preparation, tightening pattern and later retightening remain part of finishing this job.
